Q: URL(fileURLWithPath:) resolves tilde (~) as home directory in iOS 26 but not in iOS 18 A:

Solution - Adding leading slash with new URL API:

func getFileName(from fileNameWithExtension: String) -> String {  
  let url = URL(  
  filePath: "/" + fileNameWithExtension,  
  directoryHint: .notDirectory,  
  relativeTo: nil)

  // Debug logging                                                                                                                                               
  print("Input: \(fileNameWithExtension)")                                                                                                                       
  print("URL created: \(url)")                                                                                                                                   
  print("URL.path: \(url.path)")                                                                                                                                 
  print("URL.lastPathComponent: \(url.lastPathComponent)")                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                     
  return url.lastPathComponent                                                                                                                                   

}

// Usage                                                                                                                                                           
let result = getFileName(from: "~TestFile.irfd")

Debug Output (iOS 26):

Input: ~TestFile.irfd
URL created: file:///~TestFile.irfd
URL.path: /~TestFile.irfd
URL.lastPathComponent: ~TestFile.irfd

By prefixing with /, the filename becomes an absolute path, preventing the ~ from being interpreted as the home directory symbol.

This approach:

  • Uses the modern URL(filePath:directoryHint:relativeTo:) API (not deprecated)
  • Works correctly on both iOS 18 and iOS 26
  • Follows the "valid pathname" rule you mentioned

Q: What does the 'L' in the beginning even mean? C++ A:

Somewhere inr your build environment, you have either _UNICODE and/or UNICODE defined. That means the vast majority of Win32 APIs will expect a "long string" aka "unicode string" or "UTF-16 string". It basically means, wchar_t* instead of char* type string. Older versions of Visual Studio defaulted to UNICODE off. Newer version default to it on.

Q: Small question: php syntax to close database-connection with prepared statements (and placeholders) A:

  1. $stmt->close(); only closes the prepared statement object.

  2. It releases server resources associated with that statement handle.
    The database connection itself is not closed by $stmt->close().

    To close database you need to use: $mysqli->close();
    That will close the connection to MySQL.

Do you have to call it?

  • No — not strictly. PHP will automatically close non-persistent connections when the script ends.

  • But it’s generally good practice to explicitly close it if:

    • You open the connection well before you’re done with DB work.

    • You’re doing other work in the script after the database tasks.

    • You want to ensure resources are freed immediately rather than waiting for script termination.

Q: Message component of the Writer web app framework fails A:

I've had this happen before. The Message component in Writer can be finicky - it won't show up if it's just sitting there empty or if the text isn't properly bound.

Try setting it with a direct value first to test, like text="+This is a test". If that works, then your binding might be the issue. Make sure you're using the right syntax for state binding (@{my_message}) and that your state variable actually has a value with the prefix.

Also double-check that the component isn't getting hidden somehow - maybe a parent container has display: none or something. I'd inspect the div in your browser and see if there's actually text content in there but it's just not visible, or if it's truly empty.

What does your code look like for setting the message? That might help figure out what's going on.

Q: In writing a scanner in C: is my approach right and optimal? Should I continue writing it in C? Any references or guidelines? A:

I would write in C. Why do we need good string support here? It is enough to refer to fragments of the original code text. See Backus–Naur form.

Q: Is there a way to get the current track index in libvlc? A:

Empirical testing seems to indicate that adding the same file URI multiple times to a MediaList via libvlc_media_list_add_media() creates multiple Media instances that won't match each other, so using libvlc_media_list_index_of_item() on the result of libvlc_media_player_get_media() does seem to return the actual track index without ambiguity.
